name: Carta

providerSetup.blocker: Carta's API program is invite-only for third-party partners and requires provider approval for production applications. Carta customers may request access for their own data, but no customer has supplied a Carta-approved client-credentials application restricted to read_investor_firms, and its credential lifecycle and non-production acceptance have not been validated in this workspace.
providerSetup.nextAction: A Carta investment-firm administrator obtains provider approval for a customer-owned client-credentials application with only read_investor_firms, enables that application for the exact firm, stores its client ID and secret through Relay's encrypted credential flow, then validates one-hour token renewal, bounded firm reads, permission denial, pagination, rate limiting, secret rotation, token revocation, application removal, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial in Carta's playground before production use.

evidence.supports: Carta documents an invite-only partner API program, production approval, a mock service, playground, and continued own-data API access for Carta companies and investment firms.

Carta documents fixed production token and API origins, HTTP Basic client authentication, the uppercase CLIENT_CREDENTIALS grant, explicit space-delimited scopes, one-hour bearer tokens, and token revocation.

Carta's current OpenAPI contract pins GET /v1alpha1/investors/firms to read_investor_firms, pageSize and pageToken pagination, a maximum provider page of 50, and firm records containing ID and name. Relay further caps pages at 20.
Carta requires production client-credentials applications to be approved and explicitly enabled by an investment-firm administrator, who can later remove the application.

Carta publishes granular read and read-write scopes across firms, funds, investments, cap tables, securities, stakeholders, valuations, partners, portfolios, documents, and user data; Relay requests only read_investor_firms.
